```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
```

## Project Overview

This project uses EPA air pollution data from RDU airport for 2018, 2019, and January to April 2020.

GitHub repository: [He_Xiya_Project2](https://github.com/XiyaHe528/He_Xiya_Project2)

## Data Cleaning

I removed duplicate rows and changed negative pollutant values to zero. I converted dates, averaged measurements from the same day, and combined the three years. The function can also convert O3 from ppm to ppb.

```{r clean-function}
# Purpose: Clean one year of air pollution data.
# file_path: Path to the CSV file.
# ozone_units: "ppm" (default) or "ppb".
# Returns: A data frame with one row per day.

clean_air_data <- function(file_path, ozone_units = "ppm") {

  if (!(ozone_units %in% c("ppm", "ppb"))) {
    stop("ozone_units must be ppm or ppb")
  }

  data <- read.csv(file_path, check.names = FALSE)

  # Remove duplicate rows.
  data <- unique(data)

  # Rename pollutant columns.
  names(data)[c(2, 4, 6)] <- c("CO", "PM25", "O3")

  # Format the date.
  data$Date <- as.Date(data$Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")

  # Change negative concentrations to zero.
  for (p in c("CO", "PM25", "O3")) {
    data[[p]][!is.na(data[[p]]) & data[[p]] < 0] <- 0
  }

  # Calculate the daily mean for each pollutant.
  daily <- aggregate(
    data[c("CO", "PM25", "O3")],
    by = list(Date = data$Date),
    FUN = function(x) {
      if (all(is.na(x))) return(NA_real_)
      mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  )

  # Convert O3 to ppb if requested.
  if (ozone_units == "ppb") {
    daily$O3 <- daily$O3 * 1000
  }

  return(daily)
}
```

```{r combine-data, include=FALSE}
# Clean the data for each year.
air_2018 <- clean_air_data("data/AQ_2018.csv")
air_2019 <- clean_air_data("data/AQ_2019.csv")
air_2020 <- clean_air_data("data/AQ_2020.csv")

# Combine the three years.
air_all <- rbind(air_2018, air_2019, air_2020)
``` 

## Tables

```{r table-2018}
# Minimum and maximum values for 2018.
pollutants <- c("CO", "PM25", "O3")

table_2018 <- data.frame(
  Pollutant = c("CO (ppm)", "PM2.5 (ug/m3)", "O3 (ppm)"),
  Minimum = sprintf("%.3f", sapply(air_2018[pollutants], min, na.rm = TRUE)),
  Maximum = sprintf("%.3f", sapply(air_2018[pollutants], max, na.rm = TRUE))
)

knitr::kable(table_2018,
             caption = "Minimum and maximum daily concentrations in 2018",
```

## Plot 1: CO and O3 by Month

```{r plot1-data, include=FALSE}
monthly_data <- air_all %>%
  mutate(Month = as.integer(format(Date, "%m"))) %>%
  select(Month, CO, O3) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(CO, O3),
    names_to = "Pollutant",
    values_to = "Concentration"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Concentration)) %>%
  group_by(Month, Pollutant) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Concentration),
    SD = sd(Concentration),
    N = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Lower = Mean - 1.96 * SD / sqrt(N),
    Upper = Mean + 1.96 * SD / sqrt(N)
  )
```

```{r plot1, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
ggplot(monthly_data, aes(x = Month, y = Mean, color = Pollutant)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), width = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~Pollutant, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(CO = "#0072B2", O3 = "#D55E00")) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly CO and O3 Concentrations",
    subtitle = "Pooled daily values from 2018–2020 with 95% confidence intervals",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean concentration (ppm)",
    color = "Pollutant"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

I used separate panels because CO and O3 have different concentration scales. This makes both trends easier to see.

## Plot 2: PM2.5 by Month and Year

```{r plot2-data , include=FALSE}
monthly_pm25 <- air_all %>%
  mutate(
    Year = format(Date, "%Y"),
    Month = as.integer(format(Date, "%m"))
  ) %>%
  group_by(Year, Month) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_PM25 = mean(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r plot2, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
ggplot(monthly_pm25, aes(x = Month, y = Mean_PM25, color = Year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "2018" = "#0072B2",
    "2019" = "#D55E00",
    "2020" = "#009E73"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly PM2.5 Concentrations by Year",
    subtitle = "2020 data include January to April only",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean PM2.5 (ug/m3)",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

I used lines and points to show monthly changes in PM2.5 and to compare the three years.

## Results Interpretation

CO concentrations were generally higher in winter, while O3 concentrations were higher in warmer months. PM2.5 concentrations changed across months and years without a clear common pattern. The 2020 data only include January to April, so we cannot compare the full year with 2018 and 2019.
